diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.claimed_coverage: Every single-bit error in a transferred cell-voltage word is detected before the value reaches the decision function.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.common_cause_note: A fault in the front end's own computation that produces a wrong but correctly coded value is a measurement error, not a transfer error, and is covered by plausibility rather than by this mechanism.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.independence_assumption: The check is performed in AR-001, the same element that produced the value. A front end that both corrupts a value and forges its code is not covered.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.justification: A parity or CRC of the width the front end specifies, applied to every word. The detection property of such a code is a property of its polynomial and width, which is a matter of arithmetic rather than of measurement.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.mechanism: Front-end integrity code on every measurement transfer (AR-001)

diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.claimed_coverage: A false reaction rate below 1e-6 per hour for Gaussian measurement noise with sigma 5 mV, while detection of a true violation costs at most two acquisition periods.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.common_cause_note: The debounce protects against noise. It does not protect against a systematic offset in the measurement chain, which a debounce makes worse: a real offset produces a confident, repeated violation.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.independence_assumption: Consecutive samples are treated as independent. Correlated noise would change the rate materially and nothing in this corpus establishes independence.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.justification: For a threshold placed several sigma from the noise mean, the probability that two consecutive samples both fall beyond the threshold is the square of the single-sample tail probability. At 20 Hz that yields the stated rate. The arithmetic is a property of the assumed distribution, which is itself an assumption (FB2-ASM-005), so the figure is conditional on that assumption and is not a measurement of the real item.

diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.claimed_coverage: A front-end gain error, an offset error and an open sense line are detected because each produces a value outside the plausible envelope or in disagreement with the redundant channel.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.common_cause_note: A shared supply, a shared reference or a shared configuration source defeats redundancy without producing a disagreement. The dependent-failure analysis exists precisely because this cannot be dismissed by assertion.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.independence_assumption: The redundant channel must be genuinely independent of the channel it checks. FB2-SAF-ANL-000003 records that analysis and FB2-SAF-ANL-000004 records the freedom-from-interference argument; neither quantifies the residual common-cause exposure.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.justification: The mechanisms are self-evident from their design intent and are implemented in the observed source. What is NOT established is their coverage: the corpus contains no fault-injection campaign that quantifies which injected faults are detected and which are not, and no plausibility limit is expressed as a diagnostic-coverage figure.

diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.claimed_coverage: A welded contactor is detected within 100 ms of the commanded state disagreeing with the feedback.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.common_cause_note: A loss of the auxiliary return line is indistinguishable from a welded contactor at the interface, and the item must resolve that ambiguity conservatively.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.independence_assumption: The auxiliary contact path and the coil drive path share no element that can fail open in both.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.justification: The auxiliary contacts are wired independently of the coil drive, so a welded contactor produces a state disagreement that no failure of the drive path can mask. This is a wiring argument, and its validity depends on the wiring being as described, which no inspection record in this corpus establishes.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.mechanism: Contactor auxiliary feedback and weld detection (AR-004)

diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.claimed_coverage: Every cell the main measurement chain monitors is also measured by the independent divider network and compared against its own threshold.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.common_cause_note: A common supply rail or a common reference between AR-005 and AR-001 would make the two channels agree in the presence of a shared fault and would defeat the independence the ASIL D argument relies on. FB2-SAF-ANL-000003 records this as an open question.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.independence_assumption: Assumed (FB2-ASM-008): separate dividers, separate comparator, separate supply and no communication with the main chain. Nothing in this corpus demonstrates it, and the absence of a demonstration is itself the largest open assumption of the ASIL D allocation.
diagnostic_coverage_assumptions.justification: The requirement FB2-HW-TSR-000004 now states this coverage as 100 percent of the main chain's monitored cell set, which is decidable on hardware: measure which cells the independent divider network reaches and divide by which cells the main chain reaches. The previous wording of this entry carried the requirement's own disjunction ('all monitored cells, or a representative subset of at least 50%') forward, which was not a measurable coverage statement; finding FB2-REV-FND-000027 recorded that and the requirement has now been revised. The 100 percent figure is STILL not demonstrated by anything in this corpus: it is a requirement, and its feasibility as a full per-cell network remains the open assumption FB2-ASM-008. The basis is therefore still an assumption rather than a measurement or an analytical model, and this entry must not be read as evidence of coverage.

external_measures.measure: Cell-level overvoltage protection inside each cell
external_measures.why_the_item_cannot_do_it: Physically inside the cell and active with the item unpowered. The technical concept depends on it existing; it cannot verify it and does not claim to.

external_measures.measure: Fuse and pyro-fuse in the pack for overcurrent events outside the item's measurement bandwidth
external_measures.why_the_item_cannot_do_it: A short-circuit event can develop faster than any measurement-and-react cycle. The item's reaction is supplementary for these events, not primary.

external_measures.measure: Vehicle-level insulation monitoring and crash isolation
external_measures.why_the_item_cannot_do_it: The item supervises the interlock; it does not decide vehicle-level isolation.

arithmetic_check.statement: 25 + 5 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 30 + 5 = 85 ms of serial work. The fault-tolerant time interval is 100 ms, so the margin available is 100 - 85 = 15 ms, and this concept allocates exactly 15 ms of it. The budget therefore closes with no deficit. This concept originally recorded that allocation as a deliberate departure from FB2-SAF-SGO-000001, which then carried a 20 ms margin and therefore a 105 ms total against the same 100 ms interval. That departure no longer exists: FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 now records the 15 ms margin as well, so the two records agree and the safety goal's budget closes. The 105 ms was not rounded to 100 ms; the margin was corrected to the value the interval admits, and 85 + 15 = 100. The reaction chain at the end of the budget is 5 ms coil command + 30 ms mechanical opening + 5 ms feedback verification = 40 ms, and FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 now states those three points separately as 5 ms, 35 ms and 40 ms, so the requirement and this allocation agree. The independent path AR-005 has its own 50 ms budget and does not draw on this one; the two budgets are alternatives, not a sum.

hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.basis: FB2-ASM-008, a declared assumption. It is the assumption the whole ASIL D allocation leans on and it is not demonstrated anywhere in this corpus.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.consequence_if_unmet: The independent monitor becomes a second channel with the same failure modes as the first. Two agreeing channels would then be read as corroboration when in fact they are one channel twice, and the safety goal would have no surviving barrier against an AR-001 to AR-004 common-cause failure.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.interface_or_assumption: AR-005 shares no MCU, no supply rail and no communication path with AR-001 to AR-004.

hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.basis: FB2-ASM-007, grounded in the observed watchdog arrangement in the pinned source. The independence is read out of the source; its behaviour over the full temperature and supply range is not measured.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.consequence_if_unmet: A software hang leaves the contactors in their last commanded state and the software-side fault reaction never runs. The hardware monitor AR-005 would then be the only remaining path, at 50 ms against a 100 ms interval, which leaves room but no margin for anything else.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.interface_or_assumption: The safe base controller's watchdog is independent of the main MCU and can actuate the contactors on its own.

hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.basis: The requirement FB2-HW-TSR-000001 states the figure. No measurement of it exists in this corpus; the closest related record is a hardware test measure whose execution is blocked for lack of target hardware.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.consequence_if_unmet: A total error comparable to the margin between the configured limit and the last cell that must remain in service would make the limit boundary ambiguous, and the 1 mV threshold accuracy the decision function relies on would be unattainable.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.interface_or_assumption: The cell input network and its calibration deliver the stated 1.5 mV total error over the full temperature range.

hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.basis: Engineering assumption. The observed source contains supply supervision and a supply-related diagnosis entry, but no characterisation of the rails.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.consequence_if_unmet: A supply collapse faster than the watchdog window produces an uncontrolled shutdown of the contactor drivers. Whether that is safe depends on the driver's fail state, which this corpus does not record.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.interface_or_assumption: The supply rails stay inside their specified range for long enough for the watchdog to act deliberately.

hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.basis: FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 states a freshness criterion of 30 ms and FB2-SAF-SEC-000003 requires freshness verification on the external interface. The internal store's age handling is not separately specified in any record.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.consequence_if_unmet: A decision is taken on a value from an earlier acquisition period. The effect is a detection that is late by exactly the staleness, which is spent from the same 100 ms budget.
hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions.interface_or_assumption: Every value in the shared store carries an age, and a value older than its consumer's freshness limit is rejected rather than used.

hardware_software_allocation.allocated_responsibility: The front end, its dividers, the isolation and the measurement chain are hardware; the transfer scheduling, the error-code validation and the publication with age stamping are software.
hardware_software_allocation.reason_for_the_split: The accuracy and the error-detection capability are properties of the analogue chain and cannot be implemented in software, while the guarantee that a value carries its age and was validated is a property of the software and cannot be implemented in the front end. Splitting the two means neither side has to be trusted with what only the other can do.

hardware_software_allocation.allocated_responsibility: Limit comparison, debounce, plausibility, redundancy, severity classification and the request for the safe state.
hardware_software_allocation.reason_for_the_split: These are decisions over a data set that only exists in memory. There is no hardware implementation of a debounce that would be cheaper or safer here; the risk in this element is algorithmic and is managed by software freedom from interference, not by moving the logic into silicon.

hardware_software_allocation.allocated_responsibility: The shared store, its consistency mechanism, the age stamp on every entry and the message-level integrity and freshness of the external interface.
hardware_software_allocation.reason_for_the_split: The integrity mechanism is a protocol and a dispatch policy. The hardware can guarantee that bytes arrive; only the software can decide which bytes are acceptable.

hardware_software_allocation.allocated_responsibility: The safe base controller, its independent watchdog and the coil drivers are hardware; the state machine that decides when to command them and the feedback interpretation are software.
hardware_software_allocation.reason_for_the_split: The actuation must work when the MCU has stopped, so the watchdog and the final driver stage are hardware (FB2-ASM-007). The decision to act is a software decision, and keeping the decision in software while the final stage is in hardware is what makes the watchdog meaningful: if the software hangs, the hardware still opens the contactors.

hardware_software_allocation.allocated_responsibility: The independent dividers, the comparator, its threshold reference and its own actuation output. Entirely hardware.
hardware_software_allocation.reason_for_the_split: The whole point of this element is that it does not pass through the main MCU. Any software in it would share the failure domain it exists to escape. The functional requirement FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 describes its objective; the technical requirement is FB2-HW-TSR-000004.

hardware_software_allocation.allocated_responsibility: Supply supervision, the watchdog window and the reset path. Entirely hardware.
hardware_software_allocation.reason_for_the_split: It must act when the software cannot run, which rules out any software dependency.

interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.assumption_dependence: That the cell's threshold is known and that the two mechanisms are not defeated by the same event. The corpus contains no analysis of the interaction, and if both act on the same transient the pack is disconnected for a cell-level event that the item would have derated.
interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.interface_description: The cell's own protection opens the cell on overvoltage independently of the item's contactors.
interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.other_item: Cell protection circuit embedded in each cell
interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.shared_objective_or_none: Shared objective. Two mechanisms with thresholds the item does not control act on the same physical quantity.

interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.assumption_dependence: That the two items do not both demand isolation for the same benign condition, which would make a vehicle undriveable without a safety reason.
interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.interface_description: Interlock assertion into the item; item state and insulation diagnosis out of it.
interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.shared_objective_or_none: Shared objective in the fault and closed modes.

interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.assumption_dependence: That the component meets its specification over the full temperature range, and that the specification is a safety-relevant one that the supplier was told about. Neither is established in this corpus.
interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.interface_description: The front end, its error-detection code and its accuracy specification.
interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.other_item: Component vendor for the cell-sensing front end
interfaces_to_other_safety_related_items.shared_objective_or_none: None; the item owns the objective and the vendor owns the component's behaviour within its specification.

safety_goals_addressed.allocation_statement: This concept realises the goal's objective for the five elements FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 allocated to it (AR-001 to AR-005) and leaves AR-006 with no part of it. Technically the objective is carried by FB2-HW-TSR-000001, FB2-HW-TSR-000002 and FB2-HW-TSR-000003 on the hardware side and FB2-SW-SWR-000001, FB2-SW-SWR-000002 and FB2-SW-SWR-000003 on the software side, plus FB2-HW-TSR-000004 as the independent hardware path. The ASIL of each of those records is stated in its own safety_allocation and is not restated as a uniform value here: the independent path is allocated ASIL B while the main path is allocated ASIL D, and that difference is the decomposition the ASIL D goal rests on.

fault_reaction.reaction: Open all high-voltage contactors, disable charging, latch and log

fault_reaction.reaction: Open the contactors from the independent path without the main MCU
Enter the latched FAULT mode and refuse to leave it without authorised service action
fault_reaction.triggered_by: Any condition whose severity requires the safe state

fault_reaction.reaction: Force the controller into its defined state
fault_reaction.triggered_by: Watchdog expiry or supply out of range

safety_strategies.safe_state: All high-voltage contactors open, charging disabled, propulsion disabled, fault logged and latched. Reachable from every mode; what differs between modes is the capability lost by reaching it.
safety_strategies.strategy_allocation: Each strategy above names the requirement that carries it technically. The technical allocation is deliberately not uniform: the independent path AR-005 is hardware-only and ASIL B, the main path is split hardware/software and ASIL D, and AR-006 is hardware-only with no part of the objective. A concept in which every strategy were realised by the same kind of element in the same way would have no independence argument at all.

technical_safety_requirements.statement_summary: The cell-voltage measurement chain measures with 1.5 mV total error including calibration over -40 to +85 degC, with 0.5 mV resolution, and detects a single-bit transfer error on every word.
The slave link provides a bit error rate below 1e-9, detects communication failure within 5 ms and covers the transfer with an integrity code.
The safe base controller drives the contactor coils at a controlled slew rate and reports the auxiliary feedback to software within 2 ms, with weld detection within 100 ms.

An independent hardware voltage monitor measures cell voltages through its own dividers and opens the contactors within 50 ms of overvoltage detection, sharing no MCU, supply or communication path with the main chain.
The acquisition driver triggers the transfer at 20 Hz, validates the integrity code on every word and publishes validated values with their age within 25 ms of acquisition complete.
The safe-operating-area monitor compares every cell voltage against the configured limits with a debounce of two consecutive violations within 100 ms and classifies within 5 ms of data availability.
The contactor state machine executes OPEN to PRECHARGE to CLOSE to HOLD, de-energises the coils within 5 ms of a fault request and reads back the auxiliary contacts to verify the commanded state.
